title: English Language Arts (7th Grade)
description: English Language Arts (7th Grade) practice - 100 questions

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "I waited a thousand years for the bus."
questions.correctAnswer: hyperbole
questions.explanation: Hyperbole. A thousand years is an exaggeration for effect.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: Which pair of words are synonyms?
questions.correctAnswer: Brave and courageous
questions.explanation: Synonyms are words with nearly the same meaning: a brave person faces danger without fear, and a courageous person does the same - the two words can swap in most sentences.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: synonyms share meaning.

questions.question: Which sentence is a fact?
questions.correctAnswer: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level
distractors: Pizza is the best food in the world
Summer is the most fun season
questions.explanation: The boiling point of water can be measured and proven.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: facts are checkable.

questions.question: What is an antagonist in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: the character or force that opposes the main character
distractors: the author's attitude toward the subject
a word that sounds like what it means
the feeling a reader gets from a story
questions.explanation: The antagonist creates the conflict by standing in the hero's way - it can be a villain, a rival, or even a storm the hero must survive.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: Read this passage: "The night before the big test, Omar felt nervous. He took a deep breath, laid out his pencils, and reviewed his notes one more time. When he sat down in class the next morning, he remembered what his teacher had said: You have prepared, so trust yourself. Omar smiled and began to write." What does the phrase trust yourself mean here?
questions.correctAnswer: Believe in your own preparation and ability
questions.explanation: The teacher tells Omar to believe in the work he already did.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: trust yourself means believe in your own work.

questions.question: Read this passage: "The desert tortoise moves slowly across the sand, but it is built to survive. Its shell protects it from hungry coyotes, and it can store water in its body for months. During the hottest part of the day, it rests in a cool burrow underground. When the rains come, it drinks deeply and eats the fresh green plants." What is the main idea of this passage?
questions.correctAnswer: The desert tortoise has adaptations that help it survive in the desert
questions.explanation: Every sentence describes a way the tortoise survives the desert.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the main idea covers all the details.

questions.question: Read this passage: "The school garden was a patch of dry dirt when the science club started working on it. The students pulled weeds, added compost, and planted seeds for tomatoes, carrots, and sunflowers. They watered the beds every afternoon. By June, the garden was full of green leaves and bright flowers, and the cafeteria served salads made from the harvest." Which text structure does this passage use?
questions.correctAnswer: Sequence
questions.explanation: The passage tells the steps in order: first they cleaned, then planted, then watered, then harvested.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: sequence tells steps in order.

questions.question: Read this passage: "Lena stared at the broken robot on her desk. She had built it for the science fair, and now its arm would not move. Instead of giving up, she opened her notebook, checked each wire, and found one loose connection. She tightened it, flipped the switch, and the robot waved its arm. Lena grinned." What does Lena's behavior show about her?
questions.correctAnswer: She is patient and solves problems step by step
questions.explanation: She checks each wire calmly instead of quitting, which shows patience and problem solving.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: how a character acts shows who they are.

questions.question: What does it mean to compare two passages?
questions.correctAnswer: To look for how they are alike and different
distractors: To read them at the same time
To pick which one is longer
questions.explanation: To compare, line the two passages up side by side: note what they share (same topic, same lesson) and where they part ways (different details, different endings).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: compare means alike and different.

questions.question: Read this passage: "Mara had practiced her violin every morning for a year, even when her fingers ached and her friends went to the park without her. On the night of the recital, her hands shook as she lifted the bow. She played the first notes, and the room went quiet. By the last note, the audience was on its feet." What can you infer about Mara?
questions.correctAnswer: She is determined and disciplined
questions.explanation: She practiced every morning for a year even when it was hard, which shows determination.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: inferences use clues plus what you already know.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "Her smile was as bright as the sun."
questions.correctAnswer: simile
questions.explanation: Simile. It uses as to compare a smile to the sun.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: What is a homophone?
questions.correctAnswer: A word that sounds the same as another word but has a different meaning
distractors: A word with the same meaning
A word with the same spelling
questions.explanation: To, too, and two are homophones: they sound alike but mean different things.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: homophones sound alike.

questions.question: Read this passage: "The desert tortoise moves slowly across the sand, but it is built to survive. Its shell protects it from hungry coyotes, and it can store water in its body for months. During the hottest part of the day, it rests in a cool burrow underground. When the rains come, it drinks deeply and eats the fresh green plants." Which text structure does this passage use?
questions.correctAnswer: Description
questions.explanation: The passage describes the tortoise and its traits rather than telling a sequence of events.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: description paints a picture of one topic.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of a theme?
questions.correctAnswer: Friendship can help people through hard times
questions.explanation: A theme is a message or lesson, not a character or a place.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a theme is a lesson you can learn.

questions.question: Read this passage: "Honeybees do more than make honey. As they move from flower to flower collecting nectar, they carry pollen on their bodies. This pollen helps plants make seeds and fruit. Without bees, many of the foods we eat, like apples and almonds, would become rare." What is the effect of bees carrying pollen?
questions.correctAnswer: Plants can make seeds and fruit
questions.explanation: When a bee brushes against a flower, pollen sticks to its body and rubs off on the next flower - that transfer is pollination, and it lets the plant make seeds and fruit.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: cause and effect: pollen moved, seeds made.

questions.question: What is a narrator in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: the person who tells the story
distractors: repeating the same beginning sound in nearby words
the author's attitude toward the subject
the main character of a story
questions.explanation: The narrator is the voice telling the story - it can be a character inside the story (first person) or an outside voice (third person).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: Read this passage: "Sam had never ridden a bike without training wheels. On Saturday, his dad took the wheels off and held the seat as Sam pedaled down the driveway. Sam wobbled, tipped over, and scraped his knee. He wanted to quit, but his dad said, Try once more. On the third try, Sam rode all the way to the corner by himself, grinning the whole way." What is the theme of this passage?
questions.correctAnswer: Do not give up after you fail
questions.explanation: Sam fell but tried again and succeeded, which shows persistence.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the theme is the lesson Sam learns.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "The thunder crashed and the rain tapped on the roof."
questions.correctAnswer: onomatopoeia
questions.explanation: Onomatopoeia. Crashed and tapped sound like what they describe.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: Read this passage: "When the river flooded the town in 1927, the people did not give up. They built sandbag walls through the night, carried neighbors to higher ground, and shared food from their own kitchens. After the water went down, they rebuilt their homes together, stronger than before." What can you infer about the townspeople?
questions.correctAnswer: They worked together and helped each other
distractors: They blamed each other for the flood
questions.explanation: They shared food, carried neighbors, and rebuilt together, which shows teamwork.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: their actions show their character.

questions.question: What is a genre?
questions.correctAnswer: A category or type of literature, like mystery or fantasy
distractors: The last page of a book
questions.explanation: Genre tells you what kind of book it is: fiction, poetry, drama, and more.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: genre is the type of writing.

questions.question: Which is the best hook for an essay about recycling?
questions.correctAnswer: Every year, Americans throw away enough trash to fill a football stadium.
distractors: I will now talk about trash.
questions.explanation: A surprising fact grabs the reader's attention at the start.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a good hook surprises or interests the reader.

questions.question: Which of these is a nonfiction text?
questions.correctAnswer: A biography of Marie Curie
distractors: A poem about a talking cat
questions.explanation: A biography tells the true story of a real person's life.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: nonfiction tells true stories.

questions.question: What is the difference between a fact and an opinion?
questions.correctAnswer: A fact can be proven true, an opinion is a belief or feeling
distractors: A fact is always short, an opinion is always long
A fact is a lie, an opinion is true
questions.explanation: Facts can be checked and proven; opinions express what someone thinks or feels.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: facts can be proven, opinions cannot.

questions.question: Read this passage: "Lena stared at the broken robot on her desk. She had built it for the science fair, and now its arm would not move. Instead of giving up, she opened her notebook, checked each wire, and found one loose connection. She tightened it, flipped the switch, and the robot waved its arm. Lena grinned." What is the problem in this passage?
questions.correctAnswer: The robot's arm will not move
questions.explanation: The story opens with the broken robot arm, which is the problem Lena must solve.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the problem is what the character must fix.

questions.question: What is a metaphor in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: comparing two things without using like or as
distractors: a scene that shows something from the past
how the conflict is solved at the end of a story
the main message or lesson of a story
questions.explanation: A metaphor says one thing IS another to show what it is like: 'the classroom was a zoo' means it was wild and noisy, not that it had real animals.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "The classroom was a zoo today."
questions.correctAnswer: metaphor
questions.explanation: Metaphor. It compares the classroom to a zoo without like or as.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: Which pair of words are antonyms?
questions.correctAnswer: Ancient and modern
questions.explanation: Ancient means very old, from long ago; modern means new, from today - they sit at opposite ends of time, so they are antonyms.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: antonyms are opposites.

questions.question: Read this passage: "The old lighthouse had stood on the cliff for a hundred years, guiding ships safely home. When the town built a new electric beacon, the lighthouse keeper locked the door for the last time. But the townspeople refused to let it be torn down. They painted it, fixed its stairs, and turned it into a small museum." What does the word beacon mean in this passage?
questions.correctAnswer: A light that guides or warns
questions.explanation: The new electric beacon replaces the lighthouse light, so it must be a guiding light.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: use the context around the word to find its meaning.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a thesis statement?
questions.correctAnswer: To state the main idea of an essay
distractors: To ask the reader a question
questions.explanation: The thesis is the essay's promise: one sentence that states the main claim, so the reader knows what the rest of the essay will try to prove.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the thesis is the essay's main claim.

questions.question: What is the mood in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: the feeling a reader gets from a story
distractors: the main message or lesson of a story
the person who tells the story
the character or force that opposes the main character
questions.explanation: Mood is the feeling the writing creates in you: dark words and stormy scenes make a scary mood, while bright words make a cheerful one.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: Which text structure explains why something happened and what followed?
questions.correctAnswer: Cause and effect
questions.explanation: Cause is the why (it rained), effect is what followed (the field flooded) - cause-and-effect writing connects the two with words like because and so.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: cause is why, effect is what happened.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "I am so hungry I could eat a horse."
questions.correctAnswer: hyperbole
questions.explanation: Hyperbole. Eating a horse is an exaggeration for effect.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: What is the third-person point of view?
questions.correctAnswer: The narrator is outside the story and uses he, she, and they
distractors: The narrator is a character and uses I
The narrator talks to you with you
questions.explanation: In third person, the narrator is not a character: watch for he, she, and they, and for the narrator knowing things no single character could know.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: third person watches from outside.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "She was as quiet as a mouse."
questions.correctAnswer: simile
questions.explanation: Simile. It uses as to compare quietness to a mouse.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: What is a hyperbole in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: extreme exaggeration for effect
distractors: the character or force that opposes the main character
comparing two things without using like or as
comparing two things using like or as
questions.explanation: Hyperbole: extreme exaggeration for effect. (I have told you a million times)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "Life is a roller coaster."
questions.correctAnswer: metaphor
questions.explanation: Metaphor. It compares life to a roller coaster without like or as.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "The sun smiled down on the morning."
questions.correctAnswer: personification
questions.explanation: Personification. The sun is given the human action of smiling.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: What is the dialogue in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: words spoken by characters in a story
distractors: a scene that shows something from the past
a word that sounds like what it means
the time and place where a story happens
questions.explanation: Dialogue: words spoken by characters in a story. (shown with quotation marks)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: Which text structure tells events in the order they happened?
questions.correctAnswer: Sequence
questions.explanation: Sequence uses order words like first, next, and finally.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: sequence is steps in order.

questions.question: What is the theme in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: the main message or lesson of a story
distractors: the person who tells the story
a word that sounds like what it means
the feeling a reader gets from a story
questions.explanation: A theme is a lesson that works beyond the story: 'do not give up' applies to Sam's bike ride and to your own hard days too.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: When you make an inference, what do you do?
questions.correctAnswer: Use clues in the text plus what you already know
questions.explanation: An inference combines text evidence with your own knowledge.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: inference is clue plus background knowledge.

questions.question: Read this passage: "The desert tortoise moves slowly across the sand, but it is built to survive. Its shell protects it from hungry coyotes, and it can store water in its body for months. During the hottest part of the day, it rests in a cool burrow underground. When the rains come, it drinks deeply and eats the fresh green plants." What does the word burrow mean in this passage?
questions.correctAnswer: A hole dug in the ground for shelter
questions.explanation: The tortoise rests in a cool burrow underground, so it must be a dug hole.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: context clues tell you what burrow means here.

questions.question: What is a point of view in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: who is telling the story
distractors: repeating the same beginning sound in nearby words
comparing two things using like or as
a scene that shows something from the past
questions.explanation: Point of view: who is telling the story. (first person, second person, or third person)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: Read this passage: "Jaden wanted to try out for the soccer team, but he had never played on a real team before. His older sister taught him to pass and dribble in the backyard every evening. At tryouts, Jaden missed his first shot, but he kept running and passed the ball to a teammate who scored. The coach smiled and wrote Jaden's name on the list." What can you infer about the coach?
questions.correctAnswer: The coach values effort and teamwork
distractors: The coach only picks the best scorers
The coach did not watch the tryout
questions.explanation: The coach picked Jaden even after a missed shot because he kept working and helped a teammate.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the coach's choice shows what he values.

questions.question: What is a personification in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: giving human traits to something that is not human
distractors: a word that sounds like what it means
comparing two things without using like or as
words that paint a picture using the five senses
questions.explanation: Personification: giving human traits to something that is not human. (the wind whispered)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: Read this passage: "Mara had practiced her violin every morning for a year, even when her fingers ached and her friends went to the park without her. On the night of the recital, her hands shook as she lifted the bow. She played the first notes, and the room went quiet. By the last note, the audience was on its feet." Which detail best supports the theme?
questions.correctAnswer: She practiced every morning for a year
distractors: Her friends went to the park
questions.explanation: A whole year of daily practice is the clearest proof that hard work led to her success.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the best evidence matches the theme directly.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "The cake smelled sweet, and the frosting was soft and smooth."
questions.correctAnswer: imagery
questions.explanation: Imagery. It uses sensory details of smell and touch.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: What is the difference between tone and mood?
questions.correctAnswer: Tone is the author's attitude, mood is the reader's feeling
distractors: Tone is the reader's feeling, mood is the author's attitude
Tone is about sound, mood is about weather
questions.explanation: Tone belongs to the author; mood belongs to the reader.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: tone is the author's voice, mood is your feeling.

questions.question: What is the setting in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: the time and place where a story happens
distractors: the feeling a reader gets from a story
the character or force that opposes the main character
comparing two things without using like or as
questions.explanation: Setting answers when and where: a story set in a lighthouse in 1920 feels very different from the same story set in a city today.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: Read this passage: "Honeybees do more than make honey. As they move from flower to flower collecting nectar, they carry pollen on their bodies. This pollen helps plants make seeds and fruit. Without bees, many of the foods we eat, like apples and almonds, would become rare." Why does the author mention apples and almonds?
questions.correctAnswer: To show why bees matter to our food
distractors: To list the author's favorite foods
To explain how to plant trees
To compare bees to other insects
questions.explanation: The examples show that foods we eat depend on bees.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: examples prove the point.

questions.question: Which sentence shows a complete sentence?
questions.correctAnswer: The dog barked at the mail carrier.
distractors: The tall tree and the blue sky.
questions.explanation: It has a subject and a verb and expresses a complete thought.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a sentence needs a subject and a verb.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "Seven slippery snakes slid silently."
questions.correctAnswer: alliteration
questions.explanation: Alliteration. The s sound repeats at the start of nearby words.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: Which words are homophones?
questions.correctAnswer: Flour and flower
questions.explanation: Flour and flower sound the same but mean different things.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: homophones sound alike but differ.

questions.question: Which of these is a fiction genre?
questions.correctAnswer: Mystery
questions.explanation: Mystery is a made-up story genre; biography and textbooks are nonfiction.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: fiction is made up.

questions.question: Read this passage: "Jaden wanted to try out for the soccer team, but he had never played on a real team before. His older sister taught him to pass and dribble in the backyard every evening. At tryouts, Jaden missed his first shot, but he kept running and passed the ball to a teammate who scored. The coach smiled and wrote Jaden's name on the list." What is the theme of this passage?
questions.correctAnswer: Trying your best matters more than being perfect
distractors: Sisters always teach better than coaches
questions.explanation: Jaden missed a shot but kept trying and helped his team, and that effort earned him a spot.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: look for the lesson in how the story ends.

questions.question: Read this passage: "Lena stared at the broken robot on her desk. She had built it for the science fair, and now its arm would not move. Instead of giving up, she opened her notebook, checked each wire, and found one loose connection. She tightened it, flipped the switch, and the robot waved its arm. Lena grinned." Which sentence shows the resolution?
questions.correctAnswer: She tightened it, flipped the switch, and the robot waved its arm.
distractors: Lena stared at the broken robot on her desk.
She had built it for the science fair.
Instead of giving up, she opened her notebook.
questions.explanation: The robot working again is how the problem gets solved.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: resolution is the fix at the end.

questions.question: Read this passage: "The old lighthouse had stood on the cliff for a hundred years, guiding ships safely home. When the town built a new electric beacon, the lighthouse keeper locked the door for the last time. But the townspeople refused to let it be torn down. They painted it, fixed its stairs, and turned it into a small museum." What is the central idea of this passage?
questions.correctAnswer: The townspeople saved the old lighthouse and gave it a new purpose
distractors: The keeper was sad to leave
New beacons are better than old ones
questions.explanation: The passage centers on the town preserving the lighthouse as a museum.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the central idea is what the whole passage is mostly about.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "The crowd cheered, and the fireworks lit up the sky with bright colors."
questions.correctAnswer: imagery
questions.explanation: Imagery. It uses sensory details of sound and sight.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: What is a flashback in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: a scene that shows something from the past
distractors: the main message or lesson of a story
when the opposite of what is expected happens
questions.explanation: A flashback jumps back in time to show an earlier event, so the reader understands why a character acts the way they do now.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: What is imagery in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: words that paint a picture using the five senses
distractors: how the conflict is solved at the end of a story
the most exciting or important moment of a story
when the opposite of what is expected happens
questions.explanation: Imagery uses the five senses - the smell of rain, the sound of thunder - so the reader can picture and feel the scene instead of just reading about it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: Read this passage: "Honeybees do more than make honey. As they move from flower to flower collecting nectar, they carry pollen on their bodies. This pollen helps plants make seeds and fruit. Without bees, many of the foods we eat, like apples and almonds, would become rare." What is the central idea of this passage?
questions.correctAnswer: Bees help plants grow food by carrying pollen
questions.explanation: The passage explains how bees pollinate plants and why that matters for our food.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the central idea ties the facts together.

questions.question: If an author writes to convince you to recycle, what is the author's purpose?
questions.correctAnswer: To persuade
questions.explanation: Persuasive writing tries to change your mind: it gives reasons and evidence for one side, like asking you to recycle to save the planet.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: persuade means convince.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "The stars danced in the night sky."
questions.correctAnswer: personification
questions.explanation: Personification. The stars are given a human action: dancing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: Read this passage: "The night before the big test, Omar felt nervous. He took a deep breath, laid out his pencils, and reviewed his notes one more time. When he sat down in class the next morning, he remembered what his teacher had said: You have prepared, so trust yourself. Omar smiled and began to write." Which point of view is this passage told from?
questions.correctAnswer: Third person
distractors: It has no point of view
questions.explanation: The passage uses he and his to tell Omar's story from outside.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: third person uses he, she, and they.

questions.question: What is the irony in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: when the opposite of what is expected happens
distractors: the main character of a story
words that paint a picture using the five senses
questions.explanation: Irony: when the opposite of what is expected happens. (saying one thing and meaning another)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: What is a character trait?
questions.correctAnswer: A quality that describes a character's personality
questions.explanation: Traits like brave, kind, or stubborn describe who a character is inside.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: traits describe personality.

questions.question: Read this passage: "When the river flooded the town in 1927, the people did not give up. They built sandbag walls through the night, carried neighbors to higher ground, and shared food from their own kitchens. After the water went down, they rebuilt their homes together, stronger than before." What is the author's purpose in this passage?
questions.correctAnswer: To inform readers about how a town survived a flood
distractors: To persuade readers to move away from rivers
To entertain readers with a funny story
To explain how to build a sandbag wall
questions.explanation: The passage gives facts about a real event and how people responded.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: inform means to give facts.

questions.question: Which sentence is an opinion?
questions.correctAnswer: Chocolate ice cream tastes better than vanilla
distractors: The library opens at 9 in the morning
Arizona is a state in the United States
There are 12 months in a year
questions.explanation: Tastes better is a feeling, not something that can be proven.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: opinions use words like best and worst.

questions.question: If an author writes a funny story about a talking dog, what is the author's purpose?
questions.correctAnswer: To entertain
questions.explanation: Entertaining writing aims to amuse: jokes, silly characters, and surprising twists are there to make you laugh, not to teach a fact.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: entertain means to amuse.

questions.question: What is a conflict in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: the problem or struggle in a story
distractors: the most exciting or important moment of a story
the main message or lesson of a story
the character or force that opposes the main character
questions.explanation: Conflict is the problem that drives the story: without it, nothing would happen - the hero must face it, struggle, and find a way through.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: What is a simile in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: comparing two things using like or as
distractors: the time and place where a story happens
the feeling a reader gets from a story
the problem or struggle in a story
questions.explanation: Simile: comparing two things using like or as. (as brave as a lion)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: Read this passage: "The school garden was a patch of dry dirt when the science club started working on it. The students pulled weeds, added compost, and planted seeds for tomatoes, carrots, and sunflowers. They watered the beds every afternoon. By June, the garden was full of green leaves and bright flowers, and the cafeteria served salads made from the harvest." What does the word compost mean in this passage?
questions.correctAnswer: Decayed plant material used to feed the soil
questions.explanation: The students added compost to the dirt before planting, so it must feed the soil.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: context clues show compost helps the soil.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "The wind whispered through the trees."
questions.correctAnswer: personification
questions.explanation: Personification. The wind is given the human action of whispering.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "A single red rose on the table stood for love."
questions.correctAnswer: symbolism
questions.explanation: Symbolism. The rose stands for a bigger idea: love.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: What is an onomatopoeia in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: a word that sounds like what it means
distractors: using an object to stand for a bigger idea
the sequence of events in a story
questions.explanation: Onomatopoeia: a word that sounds like what it means. (buzz, crash, pop)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: Read this passage: "The old lighthouse had stood on the cliff for a hundred years, guiding ships safely home. When the town built a new electric beacon, the lighthouse keeper locked the door for the last time. But the townspeople refused to let it be torn down. They painted it, fixed its stairs, and turned it into a small museum." What is the setting of this passage?
questions.correctAnswer: An old lighthouse on a cliff by the sea
questions.explanation: The passage opens at the lighthouse on the cliff and stays there - the time is the day the keeper leaves, and the place is the lighthouse by the sea.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: setting is the when and where of the passage.

questions.question: What is a resolution in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: how the conflict is solved at the end of a story
distractors: words that paint a picture using the five senses
the main message or lesson of a story
the feeling a reader gets from a story
questions.explanation: The resolution is where the loose ends get tied: the problem is solved, the characters settle, and the story can end.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "The heavy clouds cried all afternoon."
questions.correctAnswer: personification
questions.explanation: Personification. The clouds are given the human action of crying.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: Which text structure presents a problem and then explains how it was fixed?
questions.correctAnswer: Problem and solution
questions.explanation: Problem and solution first names the trouble, then gives the fix.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: problem first, solution second.

questions.question: Read this passage: "Jaden wanted to try out for the soccer team, but he had never played on a real team before. His older sister taught him to pass and dribble in the backyard every evening. At tryouts, Jaden missed his first shot, but he kept running and passed the ball to a teammate who scored. The coach smiled and wrote Jaden's name on the list." Which sentence is the climax of the passage?
questions.correctAnswer: At tryouts, Jaden missed his first shot, but he kept running and passed the ball to a teammate who scored.
distractors: Jaden wanted to try out for the soccer team.
His older sister taught him to pass and dribble.
The coach smiled and wrote Jaden's name on the list.
questions.explanation: The tryout moment is the most important turning point of the story.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the climax is the big moment everything builds toward.

questions.question: What is the plot in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: the sequence of events in a story
distractors: words spoken by characters in a story
the problem or struggle in a story
the feeling a reader gets from a story
questions.explanation: Plot is the chain of events in order: the problem appears, things get worse, the climax hits, and then the ending follows.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "He is as fast as lightning."
questions.correctAnswer: simile
questions.explanation: Simile. It uses as to compare speed to lightning.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: What is the first-person point of view?
questions.correctAnswer: The narrator is a character in the story and uses I
distractors: The narrator is outside the story and uses he and she
The narrator talks directly to you with you
The narrator knows everything about all characters
questions.explanation: First person uses I and me because the narrator is part of the story.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: first person says I.

questions.question: Read this passage: "Mara had practiced her violin every morning for a year, even when her fingers ached and her friends went to the park without her. On the night of the recital, her hands shook as she lifted the bow. She played the first notes, and the room went quiet. By the last note, the audience was on its feet." What is the theme of this passage?
questions.correctAnswer: Hard work and practice pay off
distractors: Friends are more important than practice
questions.explanation: Mara practiced for a year even when it was hard, and her performance succeeded in the end.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the theme is the lesson the story teaches.

questions.question: What is a synonym?
questions.correctAnswer: A word that means the same or almost the same as another word
distractors: A word that means the opposite
A word that sounds the same
A word that is spelled the same
questions.explanation: Happy and joyful are synonyms because they mean almost the same thing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: synonyms are same-meaning words.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "The bees buzzed around the garden."
questions.correctAnswer: onomatopoeia
questions.explanation: Onomatopoeia. Buzzed sounds like the noise bees make.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: Read this passage: "The school garden was a patch of dry dirt when the science club started working on it. The students pulled weeds, added compost, and planted seeds for tomatoes, carrots, and sunflowers. They watered the beds every afternoon. By June, the garden was full of green leaves and bright flowers, and the cafeteria served salads made from the harvest." What is the central idea of this passage?
questions.correctAnswer: Students turned a dry patch of dirt into a thriving garden
questions.explanation: The whole passage tells how the students built and grew the garden.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the central idea covers the whole passage.

questions.question: What is a symbolism in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: using an object to stand for a bigger idea
distractors: how the conflict is solved at the end of a story
the time and place where a story happens
words spoken by characters in a story
questions.explanation: Symbolism: using an object to stand for a bigger idea. (a dove can stand for peace)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a strong verb?
questions.correctAnswer: The cheetah sprinted across the field.
distractors: The cheetah went across the field.
questions.explanation: Sprinted is a strong, exact verb that paints a clear picture.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: strong verbs show action clearly.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers."
questions.correctAnswer: alliteration
questions.explanation: Alliteration. The p sound repeats at the start of nearby words.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "Her voice was like music."
questions.correctAnswer: simile
questions.explanation: Simile. It uses like to compare her voice to music.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: What is a protagonist in literature?
questions.correctAnswer: the main character of a story
distractors: the character or force that opposes the main character
a scene that shows something from the past
repeating the same beginning sound in nearby words
questions.explanation: The protagonist is the character the story follows most closely - usually the hero, the one whose choices and growth the story is really about.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: literary terms are the tools authors use.

questions.question: Which text structure compares two things to show how they are alike and different?
questions.correctAnswer: Compare and contrast
questions.explanation: Compare finds what is alike, contrast finds what is different: a Venn diagram is a classic tool because the overlap shows the similarities and the outer parts show the differences.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: compare means alike, contrast means different.

questions.question: Read this passage: "The night before the big test, Omar felt nervous. He took a deep breath, laid out his pencils, and reviewed his notes one more time. When he sat down in class the next morning, he remembered what his teacher had said: You have prepared, so trust yourself. Omar smiled and began to write." What is the theme of this passage?
questions.correctAnswer: Preparation builds confidence
questions.explanation: Omar prepared the night before, and that preparation helped him feel ready.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the lesson is in the character's change.

questions.question: Read this passage: "Sam had never ridden a bike without training wheels. On Saturday, his dad took the wheels off and held the seat as Sam pedaled down the driveway. Sam wobbled, tipped over, and scraped his knee. He wanted to quit, but his dad said, Try once more. On the third try, Sam rode all the way to the corner by himself, grinning the whole way." What can you infer about Sam's dad?
questions.correctAnswer: He is encouraging and patient
distractors: He does not care about bikes
questions.explanation: He holds the seat, comforts Sam, and tells him to try once more.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the dad's words and actions show support.

questions.question: What is a summary?
questions.correctAnswer: A short retelling of the main points of a text
distractors: A copy of the whole text
questions.explanation: A summary keeps the main ideas and leaves out small details.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a summary is the short version.

questions.question: Read this passage: "Sam had never ridden a bike without training wheels. On Saturday, his dad took the wheels off and held the seat as Sam pedaled down the driveway. Sam wobbled, tipped over, and scraped his knee. He wanted to quit, but his dad said, Try once more. On the third try, Sam rode all the way to the corner by himself, grinning the whole way." Which event is the climax of the passage?
questions.correctAnswer: On the third try, Sam rode all the way to the corner by himself.
distractors: Sam had never ridden a bike without training wheels.
His dad took the wheels off.
Sam wobbled, tipped over, and scraped his knee.
questions.explanation: Riding alone to the corner is the big moment the story builds toward.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the climax is the moment of success.

questions.question: What does the word context mean when you read?
questions.correctAnswer: The words and sentences around an unknown word
questions.explanation: Context clues are the words around a hard word that help you figure out its meaning.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: context is the neighborhood of a word.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "His backpack was a mountain of books."
questions.correctAnswer: metaphor
questions.explanation: Metaphor. It compares the backpack to a mountain without like or as.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is used here? "The firefighter said, What a lovely day for a fire."
questions.correctAnswer: irony
questions.explanation: Irony. The opposite of what is expected is said.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name the trick the author is using.
